How an Ohio Ballot Measure Could Create a Marijuana Monopoly

The article is a long read, but the emphasis is really on the idea of the money behind ballot measures. Every time I've seen the issue of Ohio's leagalization ballot come up, I see a lot of people who are adamant about not voting for this because it creates a supplier oligopoly.

There's a deeper issue about the practice of people using these ballot measures to inject their business plans into laws, which I think is the more important reason to pass on voting for this in 2015. There are several other groups that are looking to pass a much more ethical amendment to the Ohio constitution in November 2016, which would make Ohio the only state in the country west of Colorado (right now) to have full legalization. And it would be a major blow to this practice of people subverting the system just because it requires a lot of money to coordinate efforts on a large scale.

The state attorney general just certified the Ohioans to End Prohibition's amendment (article: http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2015/06/new_marijuana_legalization.html), so I think Ohio citizens have a bit of a responsibility to wait it out until next year and in the meantime supply their much-needed signatures to the ethical amendments.

It sucks to wait, but doing so would mean that we're be spearheading the movement for all the fellow Midwestern ents.
As an Ohioan, I'm voting no. I would rather risk being a criminal than put the rights to the future of cannabis in this state in the hands of fucking investors.

It still concerns me that there's going to have to be very clear communication on this, though; given that Ohio's a swing state, if we're able to prevent the oligopoly situation from occurring I could easily see the media spinning that as "Ohio rejects marijuana legalization" as opposed to "Ohio rejects profiteers from exploiting state law for select businesses".

So far, though, the coverage I've seen on the issue by state newspapers has been very good about focusing on the 10 growers aspect.
